messages:
oliver: hi team - odd one. I was on an Australian contractor payroll via LocalPay AU until 2025-06-30 (they withheld PAYG and super), then moved to the US and transitioned to Redwood direct hire 2025-07-15. I just got a preliminary W-2 in the portal showing my US wages but also a line 'foreign social tax credit: 0'. LocalPay issued an STP summary and payslips. Will the Australian PAYG/super show up anywhere on my W-2 or do I need to claim it on my US return? worried about Medicare/SS overlap and the super contribution treatment.

sophie (People Ops): thanks for the ping @oliver. summary: EOR/EOR-like partner payments (LocalPay AU) usually aren't on Redwood's W-2. superannuation is an Australian retirement contribution and isn't equivalent to US SS. looped payroll + tax counsel to verify. can you attach the STP summary IDs or payslips to PAY-5001?

oliver: uploaded STP-2025-Q1 and payslips LP-0325, LP-0425 to PAY-5001. also got an email from LocalPay saying they filed an STP finalisation. W-2 stub shows wages = $16,200 (post-conversion) and box 12 shows code Z: 0 (i thought code Z relates to sick pay?) not sure.

matt (Payroll): @oliver we see PAY-5001. quick notes: 1) if LocalPay paid and reported via STP, those amounts aren't our payroll wages and won't be on our W-2 unless we processed retroactive pay. 2) superannuation is not reported on W-2 and not credited to US SS; without a US-Australia totalization agreement (there isn't one), contributions remain separate. 3) box 12/code Z is unusual for us; we'll review the W-2 generation logic. action: reconcile GL entries to ensure no duplicate posting and confirm W-2 codes. ETA: 48 hours. tagging @payroll-bot.

claire (Tax Counsel): tax perspective: as a US tax resident you must report worldwide income; EOR-paid income is reportable on your US return even if it isn't on our W-2. You can claim a foreign tax credit for Australian tax paid (Form 1116) to mitigate double taxation. Superannuation treatment: employer super contributions are not taxable in Australia in the same way and may be treated differently by the IRS — often they're not taxable until distributed, but specifics depend on timing and whether the employer contributions were made pre- or post-employment transition. We'll prepare a brief you can share with your CPA.

oliver: thanks. timeline concern: will payroll change the W-2? also worried about SS/Medicare showing zero on the stub - I have US SS/Medicare on my subsequent pay but not earlier.

matt (Payroll): if we discover a misclassification (e.g., retro wages posted to payroll), we'll regenerate the W-2 before final issuance; otherwise no change. SS/Medicare only apply to wages paid by us. if you were paid by LocalPay for the earlier months, our W-2 will only show Redwood wages. we'll confirm and post an audit summary in PAY-5001.

payroll-bot: PAY-5001 audit queued  assigned to matt  expected completion: 2025-10-04. :gear:

sophie (People Ops): we'll also provide a template letter summarizing what Redwood included on the W-2 to help with your US filing. thanks for uploading the docs, @oliver.

oliver: appreciated  i'll hold onto the LocalPay STP printouts for my CPA and watch for the audit result. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
